title: Experiment with g5g.xlarge (ARM/Graviton GPU) instead of g4dn.xlarge for AWS Batch
description:
User request (2026-09-17): experiment with switching the AWS Batch GPU
compute environment from g4dn.xlarge (NVIDIA T4, x86_64) to g5g.xlarge
(NVIDIA T4G, ARM/Graviton2) since g5g is cheaper per hour.

Not started -- session ran out of time before scoping this. Real
considerations to work through before touching cdk/stacks/backend.py's
compute_env (instance_types=["g4dn.xlarge"] at ~line 702):

- g5g is ARM (Graviton), not x86_64 -- the worker image
  (worker-image/Dockerfile, FROM python:3.11-slim) and every pip package
  it installs (torch, torchaudio, transformers, kokoro, qwen-tts,
  chatterbox-tts, fish-speech, f5-tts) need ARM64-compatible wheels.
  Some of these (especially smaller/newer TTS packages) may not publish
  ARM wheels at all, forcing a slow/fragile source build or making the
  switch infeasible for some backends.
  - PyTorch itself does publish official ARM64+CUDA wheels for Graviton,
    so the base case is plausible, but every backend needs to be
    verified individually.
- Would need either a separate ARM-built Docker image (multi-arch build,
  e.g. `docker buildx build --platform linux/arm64`) or a from-scratch
  ARM base image, published to the same ECR repo with an arch-specific
  tag.
- The DEFAULT_GPU_HOURLY_RATE_USD = 0.526 rate card constant
  (cdk/stacks/backend.py ~line 98, sourced from real g4dn.xlarge pricing)
  would need a g5g.xlarge-specific rate, and the cost-rollup schema
  currently has no per-instance-type dimension at all (same limitation
  Phase C flagged for per-backend cost breakdown) -- may need to become
  configurable per compute environment rather than a single global
  constant, if both instance types run side by side during evaluation.
- Recommend: stand up a SECOND compute environment + job queue (not a
  replacement) so g4dn.xlarge keeps serving real traffic while g5g.xlarge
  is evaluated in parallel with a manually-routed test job, rather than
  cutting over blind.

This should get its own proper scoping pass (Explore + Plan) before any
code changes -- flagging as a task, not starting implementation now.
